The New Sociology of Science as the Foundation of the Epistemic Process: A Coherence–Persistence Rereading of Auguste Comte
Authors/Creators
Kriger, Boris
Description
The canonical reading of Auguste Comte places sociology at the apex of a hierarchical classification of the sciences, understood as the terminal discipline because it is the most complex and the most dependent on its predecessors. This paper argues that the canonical reading misidentifies the structural role sociology plays in Comte’s system. A careful rereading, combined with a formal framework developed in recent work on coherence and structural persistence, supports an alternative thesis: sociology is not the apex of the epistemic ladder but its
foundation
—the instance that determines, for any given community, which claims will be treated as real and which will be ignored and erased. Correctness plays only a secondary role in this determination; coherence plays a substantial one, and the coherence-persistence framework adopted here explains both facts. Knowledge without social persistence is not knowledge in any scientifically tractable sense; it is a private cognitive state structurally indistinguishable, at the level of collective inquiry, from the absence of that state. We formalize this intuition by modeling scientific knowledge as a persistent structure across a composite system comprising the individual, the stabilizing artifacts, the community, and the transmission channels, and by proving a Social Indistinguishability Theorem: in the absence of social persistence, the likelihood ratio between “the agent knows
” and “the agent does not know
” converges to unity for any external epistemic observer. A corollary gives the paper its slogan:
a thrice-Einstein without community is indistinguishable from a non-Einstein
. The result is then used to diagnose several open problems in contemporary philosophy of science and philosophy of mind, including the stalemate in scientific realism, the structural prospects of artificial agents as epistemic carriers, and the ongoing dispute concerning the scientific status of the concept of consciousness. summary: We present the results of processing the effects of the powerful Gamma Ray Burst GRB221009A captured by the charged particle detectors (electrostatic analyzers and solid-state detectors) onboard spacecraft at different points in the heliosphere on October 9, 2022. To follow the GRB221009A propagation through the heliosphere we used the electron and proton flux measurements from solar missions Solar Orbiter and STEREO-A; Earth magnetosphere and the solar wind missions THEMIS and Wind; meteorological satellites POES15, POES19, MetOp3; and MAVEN - a NASA mission orbiting Mars. GRB221009A had a structure of four bursts: less intense Pulse 1 - the triggering impulse - was detected by gamma-ray observatories at 131659 UT (near the Earth); the most intense Pulses 2 and 3 were detected on board all the spacecraft from the list, and Pulse 4 detected in more than 500 s after Pulse 1. Due to their different scientific objectives, the spacecraft, which data was used in this study, were separated by more than 1 AU (Solar Orbiter and MAVEN). This enabled tracking GRB221009A as it was propagating across the heliosphere. STEREO-A was the first to register Pulse 2 and 3 of the GRB, almost 100 seconds before their detection by spacecraft in the vicinity of Earth. MAVEN detected GRB221009A Pulses 2, 3, and 4 at the orbit of Mars about 237 seconds after their detection near Earth. By processing the time delays observed we show that the source location of the GRB221009A was at RA 288.5 degrees, Dec 18.5 degrees (J2000) with an error cone of 2 degrees
